name: sluagh

attributes.attribute: the Host of the Unforgiven Dead who rode only at night
souls of those who died unforgiven, kept from the Otherworld
at war with one another, the bloody marks found each morning

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The sluagh is a name for the Host of the Unforgiven Dead. These are Scottish folk figures, but they are not the fairies. They ride forth only in the night. They are the ghosts and the souls of those who died without being forgiven for the sins they did on earth. Their wrongs trapped them in this world. They could not move on to the Otherworld. They lived in the dark and never walked in the day. The host waged endless war upon itself. Each morning the field held the bloody stripes they had left behind. The unforgiven dead stayed bound to the night and to one another in a war that never truly ends.
